ladder.classBlurb: The Fighter learns to fight in fog and illusion, leading soldiers who strike from mists the enemy cannot read.
The Fighter commands like a general of Heaven and Hell, leading armies with the authority of contract and creed.
The Fighter thrives in chaos, adapting tactics as the battlefield shifts beneath them.
The Fighter learns the brutal fighting style of the deep, every blow heavy as the bottom of the sea.
The Fighter becomes a ruler of battle, their body strengthened with ages of memory and endurance.
The Fighter's reach stretches to the horizon, every charge a march across worlds.
The Fighter learns to fight with nothing: no fear, no wasted motion, no openings.
The Fighter becomes a legend the world has forgotten, a sword-master enemies cannot predict.
The Fighter becomes the first weapon of the world, a mortal blade honed against the raw Law itself.

subclasses.ds: A warrior who has sworn fealty to demonic powers, their armour and weapons corrupted by abyssal energy.
Elite archers who weave magic into their arrows. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
A battlefield leader wreathed in ash and embers, whose banner and burnt ground punish anyone who gets close.
Knights who inspire and rally allies. (Printed in SCAG under a setting-specific name; later reprinted as Banneret.) (Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide)
A martial tactician with a pool of combat maneuvers. (Player's Handbook)
A fighter who protects allies and controls the battlefield, often on horseback. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
The simplest and most consistent Fighter subclass — raw physical excellence rather than a trick or a resource to manage.
A fighter who has studied the art of killing to its absolute limit, understanding exactly how to end life most efficiently.
Fighters who summon echoes of themselves from other timelines. (Explorer's Guide to Wildemount)
A fighter who supplements martial skill with wizard spells. (Player's Handbook)
A fighter who has sworn an oath to a dark power, combining martial prowess with hexes and curses.
A heavy-armor fighter built to hold a line rather than break one, intercepting blows meant for allies.
Fighters who augment strikes with psionic power. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Fighters who carve giant runes into their gear. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Warriors of unbreakable resolve. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
A fighter touched by the Void rather than trained by any order, striking through resistance and folding space to close distance.

ladder.classBlurb: The Monk learns to move like a reflection, stepping through mirror and mist without a sound.
The Monk masters the balance between Heaven and Hell, blows that burn and blows that cleanse.
The Monk moves like chaos itself, every motion unpredictable and impossible to follow.
The Monk masters breath and pressure, drawing power from the deep and the crushing dark.
The Monk turns inward, finding the living heart of their own body and healing every wound from within.
The Monk walks to the edge of every horizon, covering vast distances in a single breath.
The Monk learns the stillness of nothing, moving without intent and striking without being seen.
The Monk's strikes leave no memory, foes forgetting each blow even as it breaks them.
The Monk masters the first breath the world took, perfect harmony of body, spirit and Law.

subclasses.ds: A monk who channels elemental energy through their body, each strike carrying the force of the elements.
A monk who has trained their body beyond its natural limits, turning flesh and bone into weapons harder than iron.
A monk trained in desert combat traditions, using dust, wind, and disorientation as weapons.
A monk who leaves an afterimage of every motion, doubling strikes and briefly fighting alongside their own echo.
Monks who wear masks and act as both healers and executioners. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
A monk who breaks things rather than redirects them, fracturing armor and shattering already-wounded foes.
Monks trained in stealth, darkness, and infiltration. (Player's Handbook)
Monks who emulate dragons. (Fizban's Treasury of Dragons)
Monks who manifest an astral form of their own body. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Monks with an unpredictable, swaying style. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
A monk who trains around having nothing left to hold onto, immune to being grappled, restrained, or disarmed.
Monks who bend elemental forces through ki. (Player's Handbook)
Monks who master specific weapons. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
Monks who study death itself. (Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide)
The archetypal martial artist monk — every Flurry of Blows hit can knock an opponent down, push them back, or shut off their reactions.
Monks who channel radiant energy. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
